simple: Roblox players join from phones, tablets, computers, consoles, and more, sometimes switching devices in the middle of a week. This page gives tips so your game works well on all of them: support every kind of control, show the right button hints, and make your UI fit every screen size. A game that only works well on a PC loses everyone playing on a phone or Xbox, which is a huge part of Roblox.
analogy: It is like a restaurant that serves people who are right-handed, left-handed, eating with chopsticks, or using a fork. A good restaurant gives everyone the right tool and a table that fits, instead of making them all use the same thing.
keyPoints: Support all main inputs: mouse and keyboard, touch, and gamepads (controllers).
The Input Action System lets you name actions like jump or sprint, then connect many inputs to each one, so you do not write separate code for each device.
`UserInputService.PreferredInput` tells you which input the player mainly uses right now, like Touch or Gamepad, and it updates when they switch.
Show hints that match the device, like 1 to 5 on a keyboard or trigger icons on a gamepad. `InputActionLabel` can do this with no code.
Place and size UI using Scale (a percentage of the screen) instead of pixels, and use AnchorPoint to set which corner a UI element is pinned by.
`GuiService.ViewportDisplaySize` sorts the screen into Small (most phones and tablets), Medium (most laptops and monitors), or Large (most TVs).
Use layouts like `UIListLayout` to line up buttons in rows or columns that adjust automatically when you add or remove items.
Keep text readable on all screens, use enough color contrast, and never use only color to show meaning. Test with Studio's Device Emulator and Controller Emulator.

terms.cross-platform: Working on many kinds of devices, like phone, PC, console, and VR.
terms.input: How a player controls the game: keys, mouse clicks, screen taps, or controller buttons.
terms.gamepad: A game controller, like an Xbox or PlayStation controller.
terms.binding: A link between a real button (like Space or ButtonA) and an action (like jump).
terms.primary input type: The control the player is mainly using right now. A tablet with a controller plugged in may switch from Touch to Gamepad.
terms.assistive hint: A small on-screen picture or text that shows which button to press, like a little A icon.
terms.Scale: A size or position measured as a fraction of the screen. An X scale of 0.5 means halfway across, no matter if the screen is 800 or 3000 pixels wide.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on a screen. Different devices have very different numbers of pixels, so pixel sizes look different on each.
terms.AnchorPoint: The point on a UI element that its position refers to. With AnchorPoint (1, 0), the element's top-right corner sits at its position, so position X scale 1, Y scale 0 puts it snug in the top-right corner of the screen.
terms.viewport: The area of the screen where the game is shown.
terms.layout: An object, like `UIListLayout`, that automatically arranges the UI items next to it in rows or columns.
terms.contrast: How different two colors look. White text on black has high contrast and is easy to read; light gray on white is hard.
terms.emulator: A Studio tool that pretends to be another device, like a phone or controller, so you can test without owning it.
terms.haptic feedback: Vibration from a phone or controller to make actions feel real.

example.title: Show the right jump hint for the player's device
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer

-- Make a simple hint label at the bottom of the screen
local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.ResetOnSpawn = false
screenGui.Parent = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local hint = Instance.new("TextLabel")
hint.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1)          -- pin by bottom-middle
hint.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.95)      -- 50% across, 95% down
hint.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.3, 0.06)          -- 30% wide, 6% tall
hint.TextScaled = true
hint.Parent = screenGui

-- Change the text to match the main input type
local function updateHint()
	local input = UserInputService.PreferredInput
	if input == Enum.PreferredInput.Gamepad then
		hint.Text = "Press A to jump"
	elseif input == Enum.PreferredInput.Touch then
		hint.Text = "Tap the jump button"
	else
		hint.Text = "Press Space to jump"
	end
end

updateHint()
-- Update again if the player switches devices
UserInputService:GetPropertyChangedSignal("PreferredInput"):Connect(updateHint)
explain: We create a ScreenGui and a TextLabel inside the player's PlayerGui so the hint shows on their screen.
The label uses Scale, so it is 30% of the screen wide on any device, and AnchorPoint (0.5, 1) keeps it centered at the bottom.
`updateHint` reads `PreferredInput` and picks the right words for gamepad, touch, or keyboard.
We call it once at the start, then again whenever `PreferredInput` changes, like when a tablet player connects a controller.

watchOut: Sizing UI in pixels. A 400-pixel-wide button can be huge on a phone and tiny on a 4K TV. Use Scale and test with the Device Emulator.
Using Scale only, with no limits. 75% of a TV screen is enormous. Adapt by `ViewportDisplaySize` or add size constraints.
Putting buttons in corners where phone notches or Roblox's own buttons cover them. Check that every button can still be tapped.
Showing keyboard hints like Press E to a phone or console player. Match hints to the player's main input.
